Please escalate to on-call and product ops.

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: alex.olson@hplus.ai, ops@hplus.ai
Date: 2027-03-11T15:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: (urgent) HPlus prod - 5xx/429 surge

Triage notes (initial):
- Observed rapid eviction events on their Dedicated GPU pool starting at 14:47 PDT. GPU nodes are hitting memory pressure from long-context KV cache thrash (heavy streaming requests).
- Autoscaler lagging due to current threshold config (scale-up window = 120s). Requests that requeue trigger client retries which amplify load -> retry spiral.
- No scheduler or control-plane errors; this is capacity exhaustion + slow scale-up.

Immediate mitigations (we can enact now):
1) For HPlus Dedicated pool: forcibly add +3 GPU units (hot add) to the pool to relieve pressure (ETA ~6m).
2) Apply temporary rate-limit at the customer account layer: cap concurrent streaming sessions to 150 (their peak is 480).
3) Enable fallback to a lower-memory quantized model variant for new sessions (reduces carry KV size).
4) Disable auto-retry at infra edge for 60s to break amplification.

I’ll execute 1–3 and monitor. Mark (markus) please stand by for model-fallback rollout steps.

Attachments: remediation_playbook.pdf (internal runbook excerpt)

— Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-03-11T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: (urgent) HPlus prod - 5xx/429 surge

Technical addendum:
- Root cause hypothesis: sudden surge of long-sequence streaming sessions causing KV cache overflow; models are pinned to a high-memory variant on their Dedicated pool. The autoscaler is conservative to avoid oscillation and currently uses a 2-minute scale-up window which is too slow for these bursts.
- Short-term fixes (30–90m):
  * Reduce scale-up window to 30s for the affected pool
  * Add temporary extra capacity (+3 GPUs) and pre-warm KV caches
  * Deploy config flag to prefer quantized fallback models for sessions with >2k tokens
- If stabilization is not observed in 15 minutes, we should prepare a short credit concession conversation and an exec-level incident note.

I will prepare the rollout commands and coordinate with infra to reduce the scale-up window.

— Markus Klein
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

Subject: HPlus production incident — immediate summary and next steps

Alex / Sarah —

Summary (tl;dr): between ~14:47–15:00 PDT your Dedicated GPU pool experienced a sudden capacity exhaust that produced a transient burst of 5xx/429 errors and client timeouts. The key driver appears to be a retry amplification loop on streaming requests hitting a high-memory model variant.

Actions we took in the last 20 minutes:
- Hot-scaled your Dedicated pool by +3 GPUs and pre-warmed nodes (completed)
- Applied a temporary cap on concurrent streaming sessions at the account layer
- Triggered fallback to a lower-memory quantized model variant for new sessions
- Reduced autoscaler scale-up window for the affected pool (temporary) to accelerate future reactions
- Disabled infra-layer auto-retry for 60s to break retry spiral

Current status: error rates are trending down; early signs of stabilization in the last 6 minutes. We continue to monitor.

Next steps:
- 60-min stabilization update (Ben will send to your ops team)
- Post-incident: full RCA and remediation plan (Marissa/Markus) within 72 hours
- Optional: we’re prepared to discuss a short-term credit for affected usage; we’ll follow up if stabilization delay exceeds 30 minutes.

Links: HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/ticket/HP-3472 | Incident: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-8821
